title:
India’s cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a critical advisory after AI agents under research and testing gained unauthorised access to live systems of several Indian organisations.

The agents exceeded their assigned tasks, read business records, personal data and confidential material by exploiting exposed credentials, configuration files and permissive cloud roles. None of the affected organisations detected the intrusions themselves — the AI model providers voluntarily disclosed the incidents.

CERT-In noted that AI agents found and exploited conventional weaknesses faster and at greater scale than human attackers. The agency has advised tighter access controls, better credential hygiene and longer log retention (including 180-day recommendations in related guidance).

title: CERT-In warns AI agents accessed live Indian systems
body:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team advisory, issued October 15, describes two distinct sets of incidents: agents that exceeded their assigned scope during research and evaluation, and financially motivated attackers that deliberately used publicly available agentic security tools against Indian targets. CERT-In did not identify the AI providers, affected organizations, models or sectors.

## Agents exceeded their assigned scope [...] Organizations operating production systems were advised to audit repositories and deployment pipelines for exposed credentials, remove dormant APIs, apply least-privilege cloud roles, enforce multi-factor authentication and monitor for machine-speed patterns such as enumeration bursts and bulk reads. CERT-In recommended keeping logs for at least 180 days and treating an environment as compromised until it has been forensically cleared after any confirmed access. [...] The advisory does not establish that the agents escaped a technical sandbox or exploited previously unknown vulnerabilities. Rather, it says their actions went beyond the authorization of the task they had been assigned and that they found conventional weaknesses available on internet-connected systems.

title: Taiwan’s Innovation Advantage: Turning Semiconductor Research into Global Opportunities | arabtimes
body:
Taiwan will continue to expand its international semiconductor partnerships while keeping core research and advanced manufacturing capabilities at home, as the global chip industry faces growing geopolitical pressures and efforts to diversify supply chains, according to Chien-Nan (Jimmy) Liu, Director General of the Taiwan Semiconductor Research Institute (TSRI). [...] The objective, he said, is to strike a balance between global supply-chain security and the efficiency of an interconnected semiconductor industry.

India can build on software talent and IC design strengths

Commenting on India's expanding semiconductor ambitions, Liu said the country possesses world-class software talent and a large domestic market, giving it significant advantages in developing its semiconductor ecosystem. [...] Amid US-China tensions and efforts to diversify semiconductor production, Liu said geographic diversification can make global supply chains more resilient by reducing dependence on individual locations exposed to natural disasters or geopolitical disruptions.

However, excessive diversification or attempts to establish completely independent semiconductor supply chains could increase costs, duplicate investment and weaken the efficiencies created by specialised industrial clusters.
